research_question: How do airplane wings generate lift, how do the four forces interact, and how do angle of attack and air density affect flight?

sources.title: Aerodynamics of Flight, Pilot’s Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, Chapter 5
notes: Lift, weight, thrust, and drag describe the main forces acting on aircraft.
Angle of attack is the angle between the wing chord and relative wind.
In steady level unaccelerated flight, opposing force components balance.

sources.title: Bernoulli and Newton
notes: Pressure distributions and airflow momentum changes are compatible descriptions of lift.
Bernoulli's principle and Newton's laws are often oversimplified in popular explanations.

sources.title: Airplane Flying Handbook, Chapter 4
notes: Thrust and drag influence aircraft energy; altitude and airspeed can be exchanged over short periods.
Pilot controls manage flight path, energy, and configuration.

sources.title: Stinson 108-3: Lessons Learned
notes: A wing can stall when it reaches critical angle of attack.
Lift and drag depend on air density and operating conditions.

sources.title: Beginner's Guide to Aeronautics
notes: Aerodynamics explains the forces and airflow governing aircraft flight.
